_readme: Site glossary for en/ (Nginx Proxy Manager). shared = WoowTech series names and chrome terms reused across the 13 sites; terms = Nginx Proxy Manager / Home Assistant add-on / DNS / TLS / Cloudflare domain terms (upstream English UI and docs wording wins); keepEnglish = never translate/rephrase; forbid = words the reviewer rejects. decisions = the binding cross-chapter wording agreed before the 12 chapters were translated in parallel: h2 forms, data-nav labels, callout labels, table headers, code placeholders and prose examples. Companion binding table: /home/user/out/terms_nginx_proxy_manager.txt
principles: Upstream English UI and docs wording wins (nginxproxymanager.com, the NPM 2.12.4 UI, Home Assistant, Cloudflare, Let's Encrypt, Nginx).

NPM object and field names stay verbatim in English: Proxy Host, Redirection Host, Stream, 404 Host, SSL Certificate, Access List, Users, Audit Log, Domain Names, Forward Scheme/Hostname/IP/Port, Force SSL, Satisfy Any, Pass Auth to Host, Custom Locations, Advanced.
Product names, CLI commands, config keys, file names, ports, hostnames and placeholders stay verbatim; Chinese placeholders become <your-...> / [internal-...] style via i18n/_proposals only.
US spelling; sentence case for headings, nav and buttons; Title Case for product and WoowTech series names.
Second person 'you'; direct, like a senior engineer onboarding a beginner; no 'In this chapter we will', no marketing adjectives, no emoji.

Callout labels are fixed: Concept: / Tip: / Warning: / Danger:; full-width punctuation becomes ASCII; the 12 chapters use FULL-WIDTH slash 「／」 for 80／443 etc., which becomes a plain ASCII slash: 80/443.
Security wording is load-bearing: 遮罩 is always 'redact', 最小暴露 is 'minimal exposure', 最小權限 is 'least privilege'. Never soften a Danger callout.

decisions._readme: Binding cross-chapter wording. If a chapter can render a phrase two ways, use the form here. Every distinct zh <h2> on the site has exactly one English form in h2_exact - it must not drift between chapters. data_nav also covers the in-chapter TOC link text, which mirrors data-nav verbatim, and the sales/prompts/skills sidebar links (those pages carry ASCII data-nav ids that are NOT translated).

h2_by_section.faq: FAQ — bare 常見問題 is always 'FAQ'; a qualified one keeps its qualifier: SSL 常見問題 = SSL FAQ, Access List 常見問題 = Access List FAQ, Cloudflare Tunnel 常見問題 = Cloudflare Tunnel FAQ
h2_by_section.sources: Official sources — both 官方來源 (ch4-ch9) and 官方資料來源 (ch1-ch3) render as 'Official sources'; a trailing qualifier is kept: 官方來源與版本邊界 = Official sources and version scope, 官方來源與核對日期 = Official sources and verification date, 官方來源與版本提醒 = Official sources and version note
h2_by_section.troubleshooting: <Topic> troubleshooting — 排錯 h2s take the fixed word 'troubleshooting' with the chapter's topic in front (安裝排錯 = Install troubleshooting, 介面排錯 = Interface troubleshooting, Proxy Host 排錯 = Proxy Host troubleshooting). ch7-ch9 use 常見問題與處理 = Common problems and fixes; ch10-ch12 use 常見故障… = Common failures and …
h2_by_section.why: chapter-specific; translate the Chinese h2 literally in sentence case. Do NOT replace it with 'Why this matters' — that is the data-nav label only.
h2_by_section.steps: imperative verb phrase matching the Chinese h2; no invented 'Six steps to …' pattern — this site does not number its step sections
h2_by_section._case: Sentence case throughout. A colon-prefixed h2 (ch12 'DNS：…') keeps the prefix and takes an ASCII colon plus one space: 'DNS: confirm where the name goes'.
